criteria.long_description: One numerical data set and one categorical data set, each chosen from the list provided, and both shown in the project.

ratings.long_description: One numerical and one categorical data set from the provided list, both shown in full.
Both kinds of data set chosen from the list, but one is shown incompletely.
Only one data set is shown, or a data set is not from the provided list.
No data sets shown.

criteria.description: Step 2: Choose the Right Graphical Representation
criteria.long_description: A line plot, histogram, stem-and-leaf plot or box plot for the numerical data, and a bar graph or circle graph for the categorical data, each suited to the data and making trends easy to see.

ratings.long_description: Both graph types come from the allowed choices and suit their data.
Both graphs are allowed types, but one is not the best fit for its data.
One graph is not an allowed type, or only one graph type is chosen.
No graph types chosen.

criteria.long_description: Each graph has a title that describes the data, labels for the categories or values, and a clear, accurate representation of the data.

ratings.long_description: Both graphs have a descriptive title and labels and show the data accurately.
Both graphs are accurate, but a title or label is missing or unclear.
A graph misrepresents its data, or one graph is missing.
No graphs created.

criteria.long_description: Categorical data: most and least popular categories, categories with similar frequencies, and three questions of the student's own with answers. Numerical data: gaps, peaks, skewness and outliers.

ratings.long_description: Covers every required feature for both data sets, including three original questions with answers, and the observations are correct.
Covers nearly all required features; one is missing or one observation is inaccurate.
Analysis of one data set is missing, or several required features are missing or inaccurate.
No analysis.

criteria.description: Step 5: Calculate and Show Statistical Measures
criteria.long_description: Numerical data: mean, median, mode and range, plus the interquartile range if a box plot is used. Categorical data: mode, plus percentages if a circle graph is used. Work is shown and correct.

ratings.long_description: Every required measure is calculated correctly and the work is shown.
Required measures are present with one calculation error or one place where the work is not shown.
A required measure is missing, or several calculations are wrong or unsupported.
No statistical measures.

criteria.long_description: A document or presentation with a title page (name, project title and date), the data sets, the graphs, the analysis, the statistical calculations and a conclusion, neatly organized with clear explanations.

ratings.long_description: All six parts are present, organized neatly, with clear explanations and a conclusion that says what the data shows and why the chosen graphs were useful.
One part is thin or missing, or the organization is hard to follow in places.
Several parts are missing or the explanations are unclear.
No final document or presentation.

criteria.long_description: A description of the experiment that gives its aim, the event or events being investigated and why it was chosen. If a simulation tool stands in for something else, it explains what each part represents.

ratings.long_description: States the aim, the events and the reason for the choice; explains any stand-in parts.
One element of the description is missing or unclear.
Only one element of the description is given.
No experiment design.

criteria.long_description: The experiment is simulated at least 100 times with a listed simulation tool, and the outcomes are recorded in a frequency table.

ratings.long_description: At least 100 trials and a clear frequency table of the outcomes.
At least 100 trials, but the frequency table is incomplete or unclear.
Fewer than 100 trials, or results are reported without a frequency table.
No simulation results.

criteria.long_description: Theoretical probability of each outcome from the sample space, and experimental probability of each outcome from the frequency table.

ratings.long_description: Theoretical and experimental probabilities for every outcome are correct and clearly shown.
Both kinds of probability are given with one or two calculation errors.
Only one kind of probability is given, or most calculations are incorrect.
No probabilities calculated.

criteria.long_description: A paragraph comparing theoretical and experimental probabilities and explaining any differences (such as the Law of Large Numbers and randomness), a reflection on what the experiment shows, and the project presented as a snapshot with a recording, or as a document or presentation, clearly labeled with the student's name and class period.

ratings.long_description: Compares the probabilities, explains differences using the Law of Large Numbers and randomness, reflects on the experiment, and presents the project clearly and labeled.
The comparison and explanation are sound, but the reflection or the labeling or presentation is thin.
The comparison is given without an explanation of the differences, or the presentation is hard to follow.
No analysis or presentation.

source.note: Built by _src/kit/make_kit_spec.py in OneDrive 'Claude's Workshop\Math builds\Grade 7 Math S2 Sparkle' from the original 1205040-s2 spec. Sparkle = the integrated redesign of Semester 2 (Modules 6-9); the original ships unchanged in 1205040-s2. Module and item titles, order and sub-headers come from the original spec ('Affects' corrected to 'Effects'). Each of the 36 lessons is one 10-point PDF-upload assignment framing its page at https://optimaondemand.github.io/mj-grade-7-mathematics/s2-sparkle/ ; that page carries the original lesson text, the original Prior Knowledge Check as its Warm-Up tab (24 lessons) and the original VR activity as an optional note, so the separate Prior Knowledge Check items and VR Lesson Resources pages are not carried. All 50 practice and assessment items (34 Independent Practice, 6 Mid-Module Checks, 2 non-Wiris Independent Practice, 4 Summative Reviews, 4 Summative Assessments) are copied field for field from the original spec (tool url, quiz id, lookup uuid, points, grading type); only ids gain the ms_ prefix, and the short instruction page each one frames is a copy of the original page in s2-sparkle/wiris/ with the read-aloud player added (same wording). Gradebook groups: the original groups plus Lessons; weights left for the teacher to set. Weeks: the course files carry no week pacing; week numbers count five items a week in the original order (a lesson and its Independent Practice share a day).
